                                      • 1 "I am not going," said Rachel. — The comma goes inside the closing quotation marks, and the speaker's name follows.
                                      • 2 "Where did you put my calculator?" asked Ben. — A question keeps its question mark inside the quotation marks; no comma is added.
                                      • 3 Mrs Tan shouted, "Get out of the pool now!" — When the speaker comes first, a comma goes before the opening quotation mark.
                                      • 4 "That is unfair," muttered Devi under her breath. — The reporting clause may carry extra detail after the verb.
                                      • 5 "I finished it," she said, "last night." — When speech is split, both halves are in quotation marks and the second half starts in lower case.
                                      • 6 "Hurry up!" he yelled. "The bus is leaving." — Two separate sentences of speech each need their own full stop.
                                      • 7 My father asked whether I had eaten. — Reported speech takes no quotation marks at all.
                                      • 8 The sign read: "No entry after six." — A colon may introduce written words being quoted.
                                      • 9 "I can't find it anywhere," she wailed. — The apostrophe in 'can\'t' replaces the missing o of 'not'.
                                      • 10 "Well," said the coach, "that was better." — 'Well' is an interjection, so it takes a comma inside the quotation marks.
                                      • 11 "Did you hear that?" whispered Ahmad. — Keep the question mark and do not add a comma after it.
                                      • 12 "Stop!" the teacher said firmly. — A command spoken sharply takes an exclamation mark inside the quotation marks.
                                      • 13 She replied that she would think about it. — 'That' signals reported speech, so no quotation marks are used.
                                      • 14 The boys shouted, "We won! We won!" — Both exclamations sit inside one pair of quotation marks.
                                      • 15 "Are you sure?" asked Mother. "I thought it was tomorrow." — A new sentence of speech begins after the reporting clause.
                                      • 16 "No," he said, "I never said that." — The second half continues the same sentence, so it opens with a lower-case word unless it is 'I'.
                                      • 17 I packed my goggles, a towel, sunblock and my swimming cap. — Commas separate items in a list; the last two are joined by 'and'.
                                      • 18 Although it was raining, we still walked to school. — A comma follows an opening subordinate clause.
                                      • 19 My cousin, who lives in Perth, is visiting us. — Extra information is enclosed in a pair of commas.
                                      • 20 The answer was obvious: nobody had checked the plug. — A colon introduces an explanation of what came before.
                                      • 21 We had two choices: wait or walk. — A colon introduces the choices being announced.
                                      • 22 The hall was full; however, we found seats. — A semicolon joins two complete sentences, and 'however' takes a comma after it.
                                      • 23 The dog's bowl was empty. — One dog owns the bowl, so the apostrophe goes before the s.
                                      • 24 The boys' changing room was locked to all twelve of them. — The room belongs to more than one boy, so the apostrophe goes after the s.
                                      • 25 It's raining and the cat has hurt its paw. — 'It's' means 'it is'; the possessive 'its' has no apostrophe.
                                      • 26 My brother's bicycles were both stolen; he owns two. — One brother owns two bicycles, so the apostrophe goes before the s.
                                      • 27 Mr Lee, our form teacher, retires in June. — The description of Mr Lee sits between a pair of commas.
                                      • 28 What a mess the boys had made! — An exclamation beginning with 'What a' ends with an exclamation mark.
                                      • 29 I was tired; therefore, I went to bed early. — Two complete sentences joined by 'therefore' need a semicolon, not a comma.
                                      • 30 Please bring the following: a pencil, a ruler and an eraser. — A colon introduces a list announced by 'the following'.

                                      GA20 · Synthesis & transformation · 40 more · P6

                                      • 1 The boy was too short to reach the top shelf — 'Too … to' replaces 'very … could not'.
                                      • 2 Ravi apologised for breaking the window — 'For' is followed by the -ing form.
                                      • 3 Mei said that she would return the book the following day — In reported speech 'will' becomes 'would' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the following day'.
                                      • 4 The concert was cancelled because of the singer's illness — 'Because of' is followed by a noun, not a clause.
                                      • 5 She has been playing the violin for five years — A situation continuing until now takes the present perfect continuous.
                                      • 6 He finished the model without anybody's help — 'Without' is followed by a noun phrase.
                                      • 7 The soup was so salty that nobody could finish it — 'So … that' keeps the clause structure.
                                      • 8 It began to rain when we were halfway up the hill — 'When' joins the two events.
                                      • 9 He did not study; consequently, he failed the test — 'Consequently' needs a semicolon before it and a comma after.
                                      • 10 Mother asked me whether I had finished my homework — A reported question drops the question mark and the inversion.
                                      • 11 It was such a frightening film that I could not sleep afterwards — 'Such' goes before a noun; 'so' goes before an adjective alone.
                                      • 12 The classroom will be painted next week — The passive of 'will paint' is 'will be painted'.
                                      • 13 My bicycle was stolen last night — In the passive the doer may be dropped when unknown.
                                      • 14 It is such a difficult examination that few pupils pass it at the first attempt — 'Such a' plus adjective plus noun.
                                      • 15 This is the hottest curry I have ever eaten — 'Never … a hotter' becomes 'the hottest … ever'.
                                      • 16 He is too young to watch that film — 'Not old enough' becomes 'too young'.
                                      • 17 No sooner had the bell rung than the pupils left — 'No sooner' inverts the verb and is paired with 'than'.
                                      • 18 She drives carefully — The adjective becomes an adverb and the noun becomes a verb.
                                      • 19 Despite being tired, he kept going — 'Despite' is followed by a noun or -ing form, never a clause.
                                      • 20 I have not seen her since March — 'The last time' becomes a negative present perfect with 'since'.
                                      • 21 Unless you wear a helmet, you may be fined — 'Unless' means 'if you do not'.
                                      • 22 Neither he nor his sister can swim — 'Neither … nor' makes the sentence negative, so 'cannot' becomes 'can'.
                                      • 23 There were so many parents in the hall that there was nowhere to sit — 'So many' is used with countable nouns.
                                      • 24 Apart from him, no pupil noticed — 'Apart from' plus a negative statement keeps the meaning.
                                      • 25 She is the best singer in the choir — A comparative against everyone becomes a superlative.
                                      • 26 The workman warned us not to touch the wet paint — A reported command uses 'not to' plus the plain verb.
                                      • 27 I have not visited Penang for three years — 'It is … since' becomes a negative present perfect with 'for'.
                                      • 28 It was such a long queue that we decided to come back later — 'Such a' plus adjective plus noun plus 'that'.
                                      • 29 Not only does he play the piano but he also composes music — 'Not only' at the start inverts the verb with 'does'.
                                      • 30 The result was completely unexpected — The negative becomes an adjective with a negative prefix.
                                      • 31 They are building a new library, which will open in June — 'Which' after a comma adds extra information about the noun 'library'.
                                      • 32 I was so nervous that I could not speak — 'Too … to' becomes 'so … that' plus a negative.
                                      • 33 As the road is being widened, it has been closed to traffic — 'As' means 'because' here.
                                      • 34 Had she told me, I would have known she had moved — 'Had' at the start replaces 'if … had' in a past conditional.
                                      • 35 The museum does not open on Mondays — 'Is closed' becomes the active negative 'does not open'.
                                      • 36 His explanation failed to make things clear — 'Failed to' is a formal way of saying 'did not'.
                                      • 37 I did not remember my bag until the bell rang — 'Only after' becomes 'not … until'.
                                      • 38 Although everybody was tired, nobody complained — 'Although' introduces the contrast and takes a comma.
                                      • 39 The winner of the prize is my neighbour — A relative clause can often be shortened to a noun phrase.
                                      • 40 I shall not warn you again — 'The last time' becomes a negative with 'again'.

                                      GA21 · Spelling · 40 more words · P4

                                      • 1 necessary — One c, two s's: ne-ces-sary.
                                      • 2 definitely — There is no 'a' in 'definitely' — it comes from 'finite'.
                                      • 3 separate — There is 'a rat' in sep-a-rate.
                                      • 4 embarrassed — Two r's and two s's.
                                      • 5 beginning — Double the n before -ing.
                                      • 6 disappear — One s, two p's: dis + appear.
                                      • 7 environment — There is an n before the m: environ-ment.
                                      • 8 government — There is an n before the m: govern-ment.
                                      • 9 restaurant — -aurant at the end, not -aurent.
                                      • 10 rhythm — Two h's and no vowel between the r and the y.
                                      • 11 occasion — Two c's, one s.
                                      • 12 privilege — No d: pri-vi-lege.
                                      • 13 recommend — One c, two m's.
                                      • 14 noticeable — Keep the e of 'notice' before -able.
                                      • 15 argument — Drop the e of 'argue' before -ment.
                                      • 16 truly — Drop the e of 'true' before -ly.
                                      • 17 believe — i before e, except after c.
                                      • 18 receive — e before i after c.
                                      • 19 achieve — i before e here.
                                      • 20 weird — 'Weird' breaks the rule: e before i.
                                      • 21 neighbour — -eigh- in the middle, and -our in British spelling.
                                      • 22 colleague — -eague at the end: col-league.
                                      • 23 queue — Four vowels in a row after the q: q-u-e-u-e.
                                      • 24 vegetable — Three syllables in writing: veg-e-table.
                                      • 25 temperature — Do not lose the -era- in the middle.
                                      • 26 library — Two r's: lib-rar-y.
                                      • 27 February — There is an r before the u.
                                      • 28 Wednesday — There is a silent d: Wed-nes-day.
                                      • 29 exercise — -cise at the end, not -size.
                                      • 30 surprise — Two r's: sur-prise.
                                      • 31 business — busi-ness, from 'busy'.
                                      • 32 committee — Two m's, two t's, two e's.
                                      • 33 immediately — Two m's, and -ately at the end.
                                      • 34 interrupt — Two r's: inter + rupt.
                                      • 35 successful — Two c's, two s's, one l.
                                      • 36 until — Only one l in 'until'.
                                      • 37 finally — Two l's: final + ly.
                                      • 38 similar — -ar at the end, not -er.
                                      • 39 stomach — -ach at the end, pronounced 'ak'.
                                      • 40 scissors — Silent c at the start, and a double s in the middle: sci-ssors.

                                      GA22 · Editing · four more passages · P5

                                      • 1 drove — The error was “drive”. The sentence is about last December, so it needs the past tense.
                                      • 2 owned — The error was “own”. After 'was' the passive needs the past participle 'owned'.
                                      • 3 walked — The error was “walk”. It must match the past tense of 'watched' in the same sentence.
                                      • 4 better — The error was “gooder”. The comparative of 'good' is 'better'.
                                      • 5 more — The error was “most”. With only two people, use the comparative 'more'.
                                      • 6 their — The error was “they”. A possessive is needed before 'own'.
                                      • 7 bringing — The error was “bring”. After 'look forward to' the verb takes the -ing form.
                                      • 8 have — The error was “had”. After 'would' the verb is 'have'.
                                      • 9 were — The error was “was”. 'All of us' is plural.
                                      • 10 its — The error was “it's”. 'It's' means 'it is'; the possessive has no apostrophe.
                                      • 11 were — The error was “was”. With 'neither … nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'pupils'.
                                      • 12 felt — The error was “feel”. The sentence is in the past tense.
                                      • 13 than — The error was “as”. A comparative such as 'longer' is followed by 'than'.
                                      • 14 were — The error was “was”. 'Legs' is plural.
                                      • 15 tripped — The error was “trip”. The past tense is needed to match 'fell'.
                                      • 16 overtaking — The error was “overtake”. After 'were' the verb takes the -ing form.
                                      • 17 was — The error was “were”. 'She' takes 'was'.
                                      • 18 I — The error was “me”. It is part of the subject of the sentence.
                                      • 19 has — The error was “have”. 'The library' is singular.
                                      • 20 is — The error was “are”. 'Nobody' is singular.
                                      • 21 gone — The error was “went”. After 'have' the past participle is 'gone'.
                                      • 22 books — The error was “book”. 'Three' requires the plural.
                                      • 23 recommended — The error was “recommend”. The sentence is in the past tense.
                                      • 24 was — The error was “were”. 'It' takes 'was'.
                                      • 25 than — The error was “then”. After a comparative use 'than'.
                                      • 26 dislikes — The error was “dislike”. 'Who' refers to 'brother', which is singular.
                                      • 27 go — The error was “goes”. 'The two of us' is plural.
                                      • 28 start — The error was “starts”. 'The cleaners' is plural.
                                      • 29 have — The error was “has”. 'Corridors' is plural.
                                      • 30 decided — The error was “decide”. 'Last term' requires the past tense.
                                      • 31 knew — The error was “knowed”. The past tense of 'know' is 'knew'.
                                      • 32 has — The error was “have”. 'Mdm Siti' is singular.
                                      • 33 wakes — The error was “wake”. 'She' takes the -s form for a habit.
                                      • 34 anything — The error was “nothing”. Two negatives in one clause cancel each other out.
                                      • 35 has — The error was “have”. 'Its' shows the class is being treated as one body, so the verb is 'has'.
                                      • 36 have — The error was “of”. The phrase is 'could have done'.

                                      GA23 · Grammar cloze · two more passages · P5

                                      1 was · 2 of · 3 and · 4 Then · 5 Within · 6 were · 7 for · 8 Nobody · 9 been · 10 At · 11 that · 12 could · 13 than · 14 which · 15 did · 16 has · 17 one · 18 who · 19 does · 20 as · 21 When · 22 because · 23 told · 24 it · 25 Everybody · 26 been · 27 Now · 28 her · 29 where · 30 would

                                      GA24 · Standard English · 40 habits to unlearn · P5

                                      1 (1) · 2 (1) · 3 (1) · 4 (1) · 5 (1) · 6 (1) · 7 (1) · 8 (1) · 9 (1) · 10 (1) · 11 (1) · 12 (1) · 13 (1) · 14 (1) · 15 (1) · 16 (1) · 17 (1) · 18 (1) · 19 (1) · 20 (1) · 21 (1) · 22 (1) · 23 (1) · 24 (1) · 25 (1) · 26 (1) · 27 (1) · 28 (1) · 29 (1) · 30 (1) · 31 (1) · 32 (1) · 33 (1) · 34 (1) · 35 (1) · 36 (1) · 37 (1) · 38 (1) · 39 (1) · 40 (1)

                                      • 1 Could you help me carry this? — A request in writing needs a subject and a question form.
                                      • 2 I used to be very frightened of dogs. — 'Last time' meaning 'formerly' becomes 'used to'.
                                      • 3 He went to the camp. — 'Got' is not used to mark the past tense in written English.
                                      • 4 Please switch on the fan. — 'On' and 'off' are not verbs in written English; use 'switch on' or 'turn on'.
                                      • 5 I will reply to you tomorrow. — 'Revert' means to go back to an earlier state, not to reply.
                                      • 6 The two sisters look alike. — Repetition for emphasis is spoken usage only.
                                      • 7 I have already seen the doctor. — 'Already' with a finished action takes the present perfect.
                                      • 8 Nothing is that cheap. — 'Where got' expressing disbelief has no written equivalent; state the meaning plainly.
                                      • 9 My mobile phone has stopped working. — 'Spoil' for a device becomes 'break' or 'stop working'; 'handphone' is 'mobile phone' in formal writing.
                                      • 10 Could you switch off the light? — Use 'switch off' or 'turn off'.
                                      • 11 I did not go to school yesterday. — 'Never' means 'not once ever'; for a single day use 'did not'.
                                      • 12 She is taller than I am. — Never use 'more' with an -er comparative.
                                      • 13 The food is very nice. — Written English needs the verb 'to be'.
                                      • 14 That is very inconvenient. — Particles such as 'lah' and 'leh' do not appear in written English.
                                      • 15 I live in Yishun. — 'Stay' means a temporary visit; where you live permanently is 'live'.
                                      • 16 Please note the deadline. — 'Take note' needs 'of'; the standard written form is simply 'Please note'.
                                      • 17 He is one of my friends. — 'One of' is always followed by a plural noun.
                                      • 18 There are people waiting outside. — 'There is' or 'there are' introduces existence.
                                      • 19 I want to lend you my book. — You lend something TO somebody; you borrow something FROM somebody.
                                      • 20 May I come with you to the shop? — 'Follow' means to go behind; going together is 'come with'.
                                      • 21 The teacher scolded me a moment ago. — The verb needs the past tense: 'scolded'. ('Just now' for a moment ago is acceptable; what is non-standard is using it for any earlier time.)
                                      • 22 Please return my pen to me. — 'Return' takes 'to', and 'return back' is repetitive.
                                      • 23 Every pupil received a prize. — 'Every' goes directly before a singular noun.
                                      • 24 I have a headache. — 'Have' meaning 'possess' or 'suffer from' is not used in the continuous form.
                                      • 25 I will call you later. — The future needs 'will'.
                                      • 26 This one is mine. — The emphatic 'one' at the end is spoken usage only.
                                      • 27 He is very clever. — 'Very the' is spoken usage; use 'very' alone.
                                      • 28 Do not treat this lightly. — State the meaning rather than repeating the verb.
                                      • 29 Even now I still do not understand. — 'Even now' or 'to this day' is the standard form.
                                      • 30 Could you pass me the salt? — A polite request needs a subject.
                                      • 31 My mother is a nurse. — Do not repeat the subject with a pronoun.
                                      • 32 I do not need help. — The negative of 'need' is 'do not need'.
                                      • 33 She goes there by bus. — 'By bus' is the set phrase, and the verb needs -s.
                                      • 34 Be careful, or you will fall. — State the warning directly.
                                      • 35 It does not have to be done carefully. — 'Anyhow' meaning 'carelessly' is spoken usage.
                                      • 36 I have been at home all day. — A period continuing up to now takes the present perfect.
                                      • 37 The queue was extremely long. — Avoid slang intensifiers in written English.
                                      • 38 He is the better player. — 'Better' is already a comparative.
                                      • 39 In future I will remember. — 'Next time onwards' is not standard; use 'in future' or 'from now on'.
                                      • 40 Discuss the problem. — 'Discuss' takes no preposition.

                                      GA25 · Verb pairs that get confused · 40 items · P5

                                      • 1 lend — You lend something TO somebody.
                                      • 2 borrow — You borrow something FROM somebody.
                                      • 3 taught — A teacher teaches; a pupil learns.
                                      • 4 learnt — The person receiving the knowledge learns.
                                      • 5 take — 'Take' means away from where the speaker is.
                                      • 6 bring — 'Bring' means towards where the speaker is.
                                      • 7 lie — 'Lie' means to rest; it takes no object.
                                      • 8 lay — 'Lay' means to put something down; it takes an object.
                                      • 9 rises — 'Rise' means to go up by itself.
                                      • 10 raised — 'Raise' means to lift something else.
                                      • 11 hear — 'Hear' is what reaches your ears; 'listen' is paying attention.
                                      • 12 listen — 'Listen' takes 'to' and means to pay attention.
                                      • 13 see — 'See' is noticing with your eyes.
                                      • 14 watched — 'Watch' means to follow something over time; 'see' is a single act of noticing.
                                      • 15 leave — 'Leave' means to depart from a place or person.
                                      • 16 check — 'Check' means to look over; 'control' means to direct.
                                      • 17 disturbed — 'Disturb somebody's sleep' is the set phrase.
                                      • 18 spent — You spend money ON something. 'Spend' is the verb for paying money out.
                                      • 19 close — 'Close' is the verb; 'near' means nearby.
                                      • 20 took — 'Take a temperature' is the set phrase.
                                      • 21 tell — 'Tell the difference' is the set phrase.
                                      • 22 say — 'Say' is followed by the words; 'tell' is followed by a person.
                                      • 23 told — 'Tell' takes a person as its object.
                                      • 24 left — You leave an object somewhere; you forget a fact.
                                      • 25 forgot — You forget information, not an object in a place.
                                      • 26 took — 'Take a photograph' is the set phrase.
                                      • 27 make — 'Make a decision' is the set phrase.
                                      • 28 do — 'Do homework' is the set phrase.
                                      • 29 caused — 'Caused something to happen' is the correct pattern.
                                      • 30 made — 'Make somebody do something' takes no 'to'.
                                      • 31 turn off — Taps and lights are turned off, not closed.
                                      • 32 opens — A daily habit takes the present tense.
                                      • 33 answer — 'Answer' takes a direct object; 'reply' takes 'to'.
                                      • 34 reply — 'Reply' is followed by 'to'.
                                      • 35 kicked — A ball struck with the foot is kicked.
                                      • 36 forced — 'Force somebody to do something' takes 'to'.
                                      • 37 ask — 'Ask' means to request; 'question' suggests doubting them.
                                      • 38 touch — 'Touch' is the action; 'feel' is the sensation.
                                      • 39 eat — Food is eaten; medicine is taken.
                                      • 40 take — Medicine is taken, not eaten.

                                      GA26 · Present perfect or past simple · 35 items · P5

                                      • 1 have finished — 'Already' with no stated time takes the present perfect.
                                      • 2 finished — 'At six o'clock' is a finished time.
                                      • 3 has lived — 'Since' means the situation continues, so use the present perfect.
                                      • 4 lived — The period is over, so use the past simple.
                                      • 5 Have — 'Ever' in a question about any time takes the present perfect.
                                      • 6 Did — 'Last night' is a finished time.
                                      • 7 have visited — 'This year' is not over yet.
                                      • 8 visited — 'Last year' is over.
                                      • 9 has lost — 'Not yet' means the search is still going on, so use the present perfect.
                                      • 10 lost — A finished event with a stated day.
                                      • 11 have just left — 'Just' for something a moment ago takes the present perfect.
                                      • 12 left — 'Ago' always takes the past simple.
                                      • 13 have — 'Never been' is present perfect.
                                      • 14 went — A stated year takes the past simple.
                                      • 15 have — 'How long' about something still true takes the present perfect.
                                      • 16 did — 'When' asks for a finished point in time.
                                      • 17 has — The result matters now.
                                      • 18 rained — 'Last week' is finished.
                                      • 19 have seen — No time is stated and the liking continues.
                                      • 20 saw — 'On Saturday' is a finished time.
                                      • 21 has broken — 'Is still in plaster' shows the result continues, so use the present perfect.
                                      • 22 broke — 'When she was nine' is finished.
                                      • 23 have lived — 'Since' takes the present perfect.
                                      • 24 Has — 'Yet' takes the present perfect.
                                      • 25 came — A stated clock time that has passed.
                                      • 26 has found — 'So far' means up to now.
                                      • 27 found — 'Yesterday' is finished.
                                      • 28 have not seen — 'Since Monday' continues to now.
                                      • 29 saw — A finished day.
                                      • 30 has won — The season is still going on.
                                      • 31 won — 'Last season' is over.
                                      • 32 Have — A question about right now.
                                      • 33 have risen — 'Since' takes the present perfect.
                                      • 34 rose — A stated year.
                                      • 35 have tried — 'This is the first time' is always followed by the present perfect.
                                      Document 14

                                      More Vocabulary Practice — 11 New Sets

                                      Eight further vocabulary sets: similes and proverbs, homophones, compound words, words for describing feelings and character, vivid verbs for composition, a third set of idioms, a vocabulary cloze and the precise words that lift a Primary 6 answer.

                                      Work one section at a time. Write your answers on paper, then mark yourself against the answer key at the end. Anything you get wrong goes on your error log and comes back in a week.

                                      VA11 · Similes & proverbs · 40 items · P5

                                      Choose the option that completes the simile or proverb correctly.

                                      1. After the long hike, Ravi slept like a ____. (1) log (2) stone (3) rock (4) brick

                                      2. The twins are as alike as two ____ in a pod. (1) beans (2) peas (3) seeds (4) nuts

                                      3. My grandfather is as fit as a ____ at seventy. (1) fiddle (2) flute (3) drum (4) horse

                                      4. She went as white as a ____ when she heard the news. (1) cloud (2) sheet (3) wall (4) shirt

                                      5. The little boy was as quiet as a ____ during the test. (1) fish (2) mouse (3) shadow (4) leaf

                                      6. The soup was as cold as ____ by the time we ate. (1) snow (2) ice (3) winter (4) metal

                                      7. He is as stubborn as a ____. (1) mule (2) goat (3) bull (4) dog

                                      8. Her explanation was as clear as ____. (1) water (2) glass (3) crystal (4) paper

                                      9. The old man's hands were as rough as ____. (1) sandpaper (2) stone (3) bark (4) rope

                                      10. Don't count your ____ before they hatch. (1) eggs (2) chickens (3) birds (4) hens

                                      11. A ____ in time saves nine. (1) stitch (2) minute (3) needle (4) second

                                      12. Too many ____ spoil the broth. (1) chefs (2) cooks (3) hands (4) spoons

                                      13. Actions speak louder than ____. (1) promises (2) words (3) thoughts (4) plans

                                      14. Don't judge a book by its ____. (1) cover (2) title (3) size (4) author

                                      15. The early ____ catches the worm. (1) bird (2) hen (3) sparrow (4) crow

                                      16. Practice makes ____. (1) better (2) progress (3) perfect (4) champions

                                      17. Where there's a will, there's a ____. (1) path (2) way (3) road (4) chance

                                      18. Two ____ don't make a right. (1) mistakes (2) wrongs (3) errors (4) faults

                                      19. Look before you ____. (1) jump (2) leap (3) step (4) move

                                      20. A leopard cannot change its ____. (1) stripes (2) spots (3) fur (4) habits

                                      21. Rome was not built in a ____. (1) year (2) day (3) week (4) month

                                      22. Strike while the ____ is hot. (1) pan (2) iron (3) fire (4) metal

                                      23. Every ____ has a silver lining. (1) storm (2) cloud (3) sky (4) rain

                                      24. Let sleeping ____ lie. (1) cats (2) dogs (3) bears (4) lions

                                      25. Birds of a ____ flock together. (1) feather (2) kind (3) wing (4) nest

                                      26. The ____ is mightier than the sword. (1) word (2) pen (3) tongue (4) book

                                      27. Honesty is the best ____. (1) policy (2) rule (3) way (4) habit

                                      28. Beggars cannot be ____. (1) choosers (2) fussy (3) picky (4) buyers

                                      29. Make ____ while the sun shines. (1) bread (2) hay (3) money (4) plans

                                      30. He was as busy as a ____ all afternoon. (1) bee (2) wasp (3) ant (4) bird

                                      31. The thief was as slippery as an ____ and slid away through the crowd. (1) eel (2) oil slick (3) ice rink (4) otter

                                      32. My sister eats like a ____ when she gets home. (1) wolf (2) horse (3) pig (4) bear

                                      33. He is as blind as a ____ without his glasses. (1) mole (2) bat (3) worm (4) fish

                                      34. The answer was as plain as the ____ on your face. (1) eyes (2) nose (3) mouth (4) smile

                                      35. A ____ of all trades is a master of none. (1) man (2) jack (3) hand (4) worker

                                      36. Don't put all your ____ in one basket. (1) hopes (2) eggs (3) fruit (4) money

                                      37. It is no use crying over spilt ____. (1) water (2) milk (3) tea (4) juice

                                      38. She felt as light as a ____ after the results came out. (1) cloud (2) feather (3) balloon (4) bird

                                      39. The new boy stood out like a ____ thumb. (1) sore (2) red (3) big (4) swollen

                                      40. Better late than ____. (1) nothing (2) never (3) absent (4) early

                                      VA12 · Homophones · words that sound the same · P4

                                      These pairs sound identical but mean different things. Write the correct one.

                                      1. The wind ____ (blew / blue) so hard that the umbrella turned inside out.

                                      2. Please write your name on the line ____ (their / there / they're) is a space.

                                      3. ____ (Their / There / They're) bags were left in the corridor.

                                      4. ____ (Their / There / They're) coming over after lunch.

                                      5. I could not hear the announcement because the fan was ____ (to / too / two) loud.

                                      6. We walked ____ (to / too / two) the bus stop together.

                                      7. She has ____ (to / too / two) younger brothers.

                                      8. The dog wagged ____ (its / it's) tail.

                                      9. ____ (Its / It's) almost time for recess.

                                      10. ____ (Your / You're) shoes are under the bed.

                                      11. ____ (Your / You're) going to enjoy this book.

                                      12. We stood on the ____ (peace / piece) of cardboard to keep our feet dry.

                                      13. After the argument they finally made ____ (peace / piece).

                                      14. The nurse checked his ____ (hole / whole) arm for a rash.

                                      15. There was a ____ (hole / whole) in the fence behind the shed.

                                      16. The referee decided the tackle was ____ (fair / fare) and waved play on.

                                      17. My grandmother paid the bus ____ (fair / fare) with her card.

                                      18. From the top of the hill we could see the whole ____ (plane / plain).

                                      19. She took a quick ____ (peak / peek) at the last page.

                                      20. The ____ (weather / whether) forecast promised thunderstorms.

                                      21. I could not decide ____ (weather / whether) to go.

                                      22. The recipe calls for ____ (flour / flower) and eggs.

                                      23. She planted one ____ (flour / flower) in each pot.

                                      24. My shoes were ____ (allowed / aloud) in the studio.

                                      25. Please read the paragraph ____ (allowed / aloud).

                                      26. The ____ (principal / principle) spoke at assembly.

                                      27. The ____ (principal / principle) reason for the delay was the weather.

                                      28. He hurt his ____ (waist / waste) lifting the crate.

                                      29. Do not ____ (waist / waste) the leftover rice.

                                      30. The bus fare ____ (rose / rows) to a dollar last month.

                                      31. We sat in the last two ____ (rose / rows) of the hall.

                                      32. She ____ (passed / past) the ball to me.

                                      33. We walked ____ (passed / past) the old cinema.

                                      34. Our team ____ (one / won) the final by a single goal.

                                      35. He was too ____ (weak / week) to finish the race.

                                      36. We have swimming lessons twice a ____ (weak / week).

                                      37. She ____ (threw / through) the ball over the fence.

                                      38. The cat squeezed ____ (threw / through) the gap.

                                      39. They stood in a ____ (stationary / stationery) queue outside the shop.

                                      40. I bought a ruler at the ____ (stationary / stationery) shop.

                                      VA13 · Compound words · 30 items · P4

                                      Complete each compound word. Write the missing part only.

                                      1. A place where you park cars is a car ____.

                                      2. A brush for your teeth is a ____brush.

                                      3. A room where you take a bath is a ____room.

                                      4. Light from the sun is ____light.

                                      5. A cloth used to dry dishes is a dish ____.

                                      6. The time when the sun goes down is ____set.

                                      7. Someone who keeps goal in a game is a ____keeper.

                                      8. A book for writing notes is a ____book.

                                      9. A path for walking beside a road is a ____path.

                                      10. A storm with thunder is a ____storm.

                                      11. The part of the day after noon is called the after____.

                                      12. Paper used for writing letters is ____paper.

                                      13. A yard behind a house is a ____yard.

                                      14. A cake eaten at teatime is a tea____.

                                      15. A person who fights fires is a fire____.

                                      16. Work done at home after school is home____.

                                      17. A bag carried on your back is a back____.

                                      18. A board on which you write with chalk is a black____.

                                      19. Rain that falls heavily is a down____.

                                      20. A cut made by paper is a paper ____.

                                      21. Water that falls from the sky over a year is measured as rain____.

                                      22. The time of day when you eat lunch is lunch____.

                                      23. The box you carry your food in is a lunch____.

                                      24. A coat you put on in wet weather is a rain____.

                                      25. A bridge built so people can walk over a road is a foot____.

                                      26. The place where two roads cross is a cross____.

                                      27. A shop that sells and repairs bicycles is a bicycle ____.

                                      28. Someone who reads a great deal is a book____.

                                      29. Food that remains after a meal is called left____.

                                      30. The sill at the bottom of a window is a window____.

                                      VA14 · Describing feelings & character · 50 words for composition · P5

                                      Every one of these words can replace a tired word such as 'happy', 'sad' or 'angry' in a composition. Choose the best fit.

                                      1. After weeks of practice, Devi was ____ when she heard she had come first, and could not stop grinning. (1) elated (2) content (3) amused (4) nervous

                                      2. He was ____ rather than excited about the prize, as he had expected it. (1) furious (2) indifferent (3) hysterical (4) astonished

                                      3. The loss left her ____ for days. (1) dejected (2) irritated (3) startled (4) bashful

                                      4. The referee's decision went against his team and left the coach ____. (1) seething (2) sheepish (3) wistful (4) delighted

                                      5. She gave a ____ smile after admitting she had forgotten. (1) sheepish (2) radiant (3) ferocious (4) solemn

                                      6. The little boy was ____ by the size of the hall. (1) overawed (2) annoyed (3) amused (4) bored

                                      7. He looked ____ at the photograph of his old school. (1) wistfully (2) wistful (3) wistfulness (4) wisely

                                      8. Her ____ tone made everyone stop talking at once. (1) stern (2) timid (3) cheery (4) vague

                                      9. The boy was ____ about his chances and told everybody so. (1) modest (2) boastful (3) anxious (4) hesitant

                                      10. Despite winning, she remained ____ about her achievement. (1) modest (2) arrogant (3) smug (4) vain

                                      11. The ____ child hid behind her mother's legs. (1) timid (2) brazen (3) rowdy (4) reckless

                                      12. He was ____ enough to enter the burning flat. (1) foolhardy (2) cautious (3) prudent (4) timid

                                      13. She is a ____ worker who never leaves a task unfinished. (1) diligent (2) idle (3) careless (4) hasty

                                      14. His ____ reply surprised us, as he is usually so polite. (1) curt (2) gracious (3) courteous (4) gentle

                                      15. The old lady was ____ to everyone who passed her stall, greeting each one with a smile and a joke. (1) genial (2) hostile (3) aloof (4) surly

                                      16. He remained ____ throughout the argument and never raised his voice. (1) composed (2) frantic (3) flustered (4) agitated

                                      17. The news left her ____ and unable to speak. (1) dumbfounded (2) delighted (3) attentive (4) diligent

                                      18. The children grew ____ as the wait went on. (1) restless (2) serene (3) placid (4) content

                                      19. His ____ behaviour at the museum embarrassed his parents. (1) unruly (2) impeccable (3) exemplary (4) commendable

                                      20. She was ____ about the missing money and questioned everybody. (1) suspicious (2) trusting (3) oblivious (4) carefree

                                      21. The dog's owner was ____ when it was found unhurt. (1) overjoyed (2) melancholy (3) sullen (4) resentful

                                      22. He wore a ____ expression all through the funeral. (1) solemn (2) flippant (3) jubilant (4) playful

                                      23. The boy was ____ after being left out of the team. (1) resentful (2) grateful (3) content (4) elated

                                      24. Her ____ manner put the nervous new pupil at ease. (1) reassuring (2) intimidating (3) abrupt (4) indifferent

                                      25. He was ____ to admit that he had been wrong. (1) reluctant (2) eager (3) impatient (4) keen

                                      26. The ____ crowd pushed towards the stage. (1) frenzied (2) orderly (3) docile (4) subdued

                                      27. After the long illness she looked ____ but cheerful. (1) frail (2) robust (3) sturdy (4) hearty

                                      28. His ____ questions showed he had read the whole book. (1) perceptive (2) trivial (3) idle (4) vague

                                      29. She was ____ by the unfairness of the decision. (1) indignant (2) amused (3) flattered (4) soothed

                                      30. The ____ boy shared his lunch without being asked. (1) considerate (2) selfish (3) grudging (4) thoughtless

                                      31. He felt a ____ sense of guilt long afterwards. (1) nagging (2) fleeting (3) trivial (4) momentary

                                      32. Her ____ laughter filled the corridor, and soon everybody else was laughing too. (1) infectious (2) grating (3) hollow (4) forced

                                      33. The ____ silence after the announcement was worse than shouting. (1) stunned (2) comfortable (3) companionable (4) brief

                                      34. He is ____ about his stamp collection and can talk of nothing else. (1) fanatical (2) casual (3) lukewarm (4) half-hearted

                                      35. She gave a ____ nod, plainly annoyed at being stopped, and walked on. (1) grudging (2) generous (3) warm (4) enthusiastic

                                      36. The ____ old man refused all offers of help. (1) obstinate (2) amenable (3) compliant (4) obliging

                                      37. His face was ____ with pride as his daughter collected the trophy. (1) beaming (2) clouded (3) drawn (4) ashen

                                      38. She was ____ at having forgotten her friend's birthday. (1) mortified (2) delighted (3) indifferent (4) relieved

                                      39. The team was ____ after losing four matches in a row. (1) demoralised (2) buoyant (3) spirited (4) confident

                                      40. He is ____ enough to notice when somebody is upset. (1) observant (2) oblivious (3) inattentive (4) absent-minded

                                      41. The ____ cat would not come near anybody. (1) wary (2) affectionate (3) trusting (4) docile

                                      42. Her ____ apology did not convince anyone. (1) half-hearted (2) heartfelt (3) sincere (4) earnest

                                      43. He was ____ with relief when his sister answered the phone. (1) weak (2) stiff (3) firm (4) brisk

                                      44. The ____ boy volunteered for every duty. (1) obliging (2) grudging (3) surly (4) sullen

                                      45. She was ____ by the kindness of a stranger. (1) humbled (2) insulted (3) irritated (4) bored

                                      46. His ____ remarks upset the whole group. (1) tactless (2) tactful (3) diplomatic (4) sensitive

                                      47. The ____ pupil asked to redo the work she had rushed. (1) conscientious (2) slapdash (3) negligent (4) indifferent

                                      48. He felt ____ about the whole affair and changed the subject. (1) uneasy (2) elated (3) jubilant (4) smug

                                      49. Her ____ gaze never left the door. (1) unwavering (2) wandering (3) idle (4) casual

                                      50. He was ____ that nobody had noticed his mistake. (1) thankful (2) aggrieved (3) affronted (4) outraged

                                      VA16 · Idioms in context (set 3) · 40 items · P6

                                      Choose the meaning of the idiom as it is used in the sentence.

                                      14. After the scandal, the minister was left to face the music. (1) accept the consequences (2) attend a concert (3) make a speech (4) receive praise

                                      15. My mother turned a blind eye to the biscuit tin being emptied. (1) pretended not to notice (2) could not see (3) was very angry (4) counted them

                                      16. The two shops are cutting corners to keep prices low. (1) doing things cheaply and badly (2) trimming paper (3) closing early (4) working hard

                                      17. He has been burning the midnight oil before the examination. (1) studying late at night (2) wasting money (3) cooking at night (4) sleeping badly

                                      18. That excuse does not hold water. (1) is not convincing (2) is watertight (3) is too wet (4) is very clever

                                      19. She got cold feet just before the audition. (1) became nervous (2) felt unwell (3) arrived late (4) grew excited

                                      20. The two of them see eye to eye on almost nothing. (1) agree (2) look alike (3) meet often (4) argue politely

                                      21. His remark about her cooking really put his foot in it. (1) caused offence by mistake (2) solved the problem (3) made everyone laugh (4) ended the meal

                                      22. The team was over the moon after reaching the final. (1) delighted (2) exhausted (3) confused (4) disappointed

                                      23. I smell a rat in this arrangement. (1) suspect something dishonest (2) notice a bad smell (3) see an animal (4) feel unwell

                                      24. Our plans went up in smoke when the venue was flooded. (1) came to nothing (2) caught fire (3) were improved (4) were postponed

                                      25. The new rule has caused a storm in a teacup. (1) a fuss about something small (2) a serious crisis (3) a rainy day (4) a broken cup

                                      26. He was caught red-handed taking the coins. (1) in the act (2) with dirty hands (3) with an injury (4) by surprise

                                      27. Winning that match was a feather in her cap. (1) an achievement to be proud of (2) a lucky accident (3) a small reward (4) a hat decoration

                                      28. The two sisters are as thick as thieves. (1) very close (2) quite dishonest (3) rather slow (4) often apart

                                      29. He bit off more than he could chew by joining four clubs. (1) took on too much (2) ate too quickly (3) spoke too soon (4) spent too much

                                      30. Their argument was just a drop in the ocean compared with the real problem. (1) a tiny part (2) the main cause (3) a deep matter (4) a wet mess

                                      31. The prefect turned the tables on his accusers. (1) reversed the situation (2) moved the furniture (3) left the room (4) apologised

                                      32. She always keeps her cards close to her chest. (1) does not reveal her plans (2) plays games often (3) holds things tightly (4) feels unwell

                                      33. The new timetable has thrown a spanner in the works. (1) caused a problem (2) fixed the machine (3) saved time (4) pleased everyone

                                      34. He is a chip off the old block. (1) very like his father (2) a piece of wood (3) a difficult person (4) the youngest child

                                      35. We will have to play it by ear on the day. (1) decide as we go (2) listen carefully (3) practise music (4) follow the plan

                                      36. Whether pupils may use their phones during breaks is a grey area in the rules. (1) something unclear (2) a dull subject (3) an old rule (4) a serious offence

                                      37. After the third delay, we were at the end of our tether. (1) out of patience (2) at the finish line (3) very tired (4) nearly there

                                      38. He let sleeping dogs lie and said nothing about the old quarrel. (1) avoided reopening a problem (2) walked past the animals (3) stayed very quiet (4) forgot completely

                                      39. The captain was thrown in at the deep end on her first match. (1) given a hard task with no preparation (2) pushed into a pool (3) left out of the team (4) given an easy start

                                      40. The video was unknown on Monday; by Friday she had become famous overnight. (1) suddenly (2) slowly (3) secretly (4) easily
